items.title: Project sidebar
items.summary: One sidebar organised by project replaces the left rail and the five separate route sidebars (chat, docs, design, issues, agents). Every project shows its branches, and every branch shows its decks and what is open in them.

features.name: Projects tree
features.what: Before: the left rail had one button per route, and each route had its own sidebar. Now: one tree lists every project, its branches (worktrees) and their chats, canvases and terminals. Clicking a row runs the app's own navigation.
features.how: Click a project row to fold or unfold it. Click a chat, canvas or terminal row to open it. The small + on a project starts a new worktree.

features.name: Search
features.what: Before: each sidebar had its own search, or none. Now: one search box at the top filters the whole tree. A row stays when it or something inside it matches, and its parents open.
features.how: Click the search box and type. Backspace to clear.

media.caption: Typing 'csv' keeps only the matching branch and chat (fixture)
Typing 'csv' keeps only the matching branch and chat (fixture)
Typing 'csv' keeps only the matching branch and chat (fixture)

features.name: Issues, Agents, Docs and Organization rows
features.what: Before: Issues, Agents and Docs were route buttons in the rail. Now: they are rows at the top of the sidebar and under each project, and 'Organization' holds the ones with no project link. Data comes from read-only queries to the app's own backend.
features.how: Click a row to open it. Cmd+click opens a doc, issue or agent as a tab next to the chat.

media.caption: Top of the sidebar. The Issues, Agents and Docs rows need real backend data, so they do not show in the fixture (fixture)

features.video: pending: needs the real app (backend data for docs, issues and agents)

features.name: Decks under branches
features.what: Before: decks (pages with their own pane layout) had no place in any sidebar. Now: each branch card lists its decks. The active deck is open and shows what is on screen; the other decks are compact rows.
features.how: Click a deck row to switch to it. Click its chevron on the right to open or fold its rows. The + on the branch makes a new deck.

features.name: Collapsed deck rows
features.what: Now: a deck that is not open is one compact row. It shows its number and a small pill: status icons (done, running, unread), the provider of the first chat, '+N' for more, then icons for other tabs (canvas, terminal, browser, file).
features.how: Hover a row to see its chevron. Click the row to switch, the chevron to open it.

media.caption: Decks 02 and 03 as compact rows with their pills (fixture)

features.name: Deck menu
features.what: Now: right-click on a deck row opens a small menu with Rename and Remove deck. Remove asks first, in place ('Its 2 tabs go back to deck 01'), with Cancel focused. The tabs of a removed deck join the active deck.
features.how: Right-click a deck row. Enter removes, Esc or Cancel keeps the deck. Double-click on a deck name renames it.

features.name: New worktree picker
features.what: Before: the project + created a worktree with an auto name. Now: the + opens a small picker with a search field, 'New branch' (from main), the other local and remote branches, and the branches that already have a card ('switch').
features.how: Click the + on a project. Type to filter. Pick a branch to open it in a new worktree, or pick 'switch' to jump to its card. Esc closes.

features.name: Split pane rows
features.what: Before: nothing in the sidebar knew about the split view or the dock panes. Now: the branch card lists every pane on screen (each side of the split, each dock pane) with its active tab, in screen order. Rows of one pane are linked by a thin line, and hovering a row flashes its pane in the window.
features.how: Hover a row to see its pane outlined. Click a row to bring that tab forward on its own side without closing the split.

features.name: Drop a tab on + to open a new worktree
features.what: Now: while you drag a tab, every project + appears. Dropping the tab on one makes a new worktree for that project and moves the tab into it. The new card slides in with a short highlight, and the dock's undo plays it backwards.
features.how: Drag a tab from a tab bar or a dock pane over the + of a project (it turns into a 'New workspace' pill) and release.

features.name: Terminal agents as agent rows
features.what: Now: a terminal that runs an agent CLI (Claude Code, Codex) is listed as an agent session, with a status, the provider logo, the task title and a 'CLI' badge, not as a plain terminal. The mod reads the tab title, or the visible terminal screen.

features.name: Footer, settings and account
features.what: Now: the bottom of the sidebar hosts the plan usage line (from the usage-bar mod). Settings and the account avatar sit in the title bar next to the sidebar switch.

features.name: Collapsed sidebar
features.what: Now: the sidebar follows the app's own 'Toggle left panel' button and Cmd+B. Collapsed, the column goes away and the workspace takes its width back; expanded, it returns.
features.how: Click Toggle left panel in the title bar, or press Cmd+B.

features.name: Always the only sidebar
features.what: Before: a title bar switch cycled this sidebar, the native Chats sidebar and the app's own. Now: the project sidebar is the only one, with no switch. The native route sidebars stay mounted but hidden, so they keep working.
features.how: Nothing to do. localStorage "rtd.projectSidebar.hideNative" = "off" shows the native sidebars again.

features.name: Context menus
features.what: Before: right-click did nothing in the sidebar. Now: chats, projects and worktrees have Orca-style menus: Open, Open in split view or new window, Move to deck, Rename, Archive or Delete for a chat; New workspace, New worktree, Open in Finder, Editor or Terminal, Copy path for a project; new chat, canvas, doc, issue, terminal or browser, Copy branch and Pin for a worktree.
features.how: Right-click a chat, a project or a worktree card.

features.name: Worktree cards on one line
features.what: Before: each worktree card had a second line with its path and tab icons. Now: a card is one line: dot, name, the primary chip and +. A branch whose name differs shows in the tooltip.

media.caption: Worktree cards on one line, decks under them (fixture)

features.name: Green status dot
features.what: The dot is green for every worktree that is ready, primary or not, and pulses while a session runs. It is gray only when the worktree is not available.
features.how: Hover the dot to read its state.

items.title: Sidebar chats
items.summary: Every chat tab of a workspace shows in the native Chats sidebar, nested under the chat it belongs to. The original app left out chats opened with the + of the tab bar, in the split view, in a window or in a dock pane.

features.name: Tabs nested under their chat
features.what: Before: chats opened with the + of the center tab bar (and those in split view, windows, dock panes or CLI mode) had no row. Now: each shows as a child row under its chat, with a status icon, the provider logo, a title, a badge ('split', 'window', 'CLI') and the time.
features.how: Click a child row to open that chat, in its window or pane when it lives there.

features.name: Status and location badges
features.what: Now: a small gray dot is a finished chat, a dashed spinning circle is a running one, a blue dot is unread, a yellow dot waits for your answer, a hollow dot is a draft.

features.name: Fold button
features.what: Now: the parent row gets a round chevron button on the right, in place of its time. It folds and unfolds its children, and the state is remembered.
features.how: Hover the parent row and click the chevron.

features.name: New chats appear by themselves
features.what: Now: a chat opened with the + of the tab bar shows up nested under its owner right away, without reloading anything.
features.how: Open a new chat with the + in the center tab bar.

media.caption: A new child row 'Tag cleanup ideas' under its owner chat (fixture)

features.name: Workspace card per branch
features.what: Now: each workspace (a local checkout or a worktree) gets a card header with a status dot (green while a chat runs), the branch in bold, a 'primary' badge for the local checkout, and its short path. The card's border contains the workspace row and all its chats.
features.how: Click the header to select the workspace. Right-click opens the app's own workspace menu.

items.title: Plan usage
items.summary: Shows how much of your Claude and Codex plan is used (not the context window), in two forms: rings in the left rail, or one compact line in the project sidebar footer. Hovering opens a popover with every window.

features.name: Usage rings
features.what: Before: no plan usage anywhere. Now: two rings above the bug button in the rail, Claude on top and Codex below. The fill is the percent used of the shortest window; the centre is the time until reset (4h, 5d, 28m).
features.how: Hover the rings to open the popover. A click pins it.

media.caption: Two usage rings in the rail above the bug button (fixture)
Hovering the rings opens the usage popover (fixture)
Hovering the rings opens the usage popover (fixture)

features.name: Footer usage line
features.what: Now: when the project sidebar is on, the rings give way to one line in its footer: Claude's percent and time left, then Codex's, then a refresh arrow.
features.how: Hover the line to open the popover.

media.caption: The usage line at the bottom of the sidebar (fixture)

features.name: Usage popover and footer line
features.what: Now: hover (or click) opens a 'Usage' popover upward, with 'Updated … ago' and a refresh button. Each provider lists up to three windows, shortest first, with a thin bar, the percent and the time to reset. Bars turn amber from 80% and red from 95%.
features.how: Hover the line or the rings. Click pins it; click again, Esc or a click outside closes it.

media.caption: The popover with Claude and Codex windows (fixture)
The popover with Claude and Codex windows (fixture)
The popover with Claude and Codex windows (fixture)

features.name: Per-model weekly limits
features.what: Now: a small helper script asks the installed Claude CLI for the weekly limit of each model (for example Fable). It sends no message, reads no token and writes one local file that the popover reads. It runs when the popover opens with old data, and every 15 minutes.
features.how: Automatic. To run it by hand, with HOME set to your real home folder: node feature/bin/claude-usage-oauth.mjs

features.video: n/a: background helper, only its result is visible
